name: GPU cluster (10 SIMT GPUs, one host bus)

blocks.name: cluster_addr
blocks.description: Combinational. addr is a 32-bit address. slot is addr bits 24:21 (4 bits). local_addr is addr with bits 24:21 set to 0 and every other bit unchanged. No clock, no reset, no state.

blocks.name: cluster_fan
blocks.description: Combinational. host_en is a bus request; slot (4 bits) names the core it is for. en0 .. en9 are one bit each: en<k> is 1 when host_en is 1 and slot is k or 15 (slot 15 is every core), and 0 otherwise. A slot from 10 to 14 names no core: every output is 0. No clock, no reset, no state.

blocks.name: cluster_rmux
blocks.description: The read data of 10 cores on one bus. A core answers a read one cycle after the request, so the multiplexer remembers which core the request was for. One register, slot_r (4 bits): at each rising clock edge it becomes 0 when rst is 1, else takes slot when host_en is 1 and host_we is 0 (a read request), else keeps its value. sel is slot_r, except that slot_r = 15 gives sel = 0. rdata is rdata<sel> and rvalid is rvalid<sel> when sel is from 0 to 9 (the inputs rdata0 .. rdata9, 32 bits each, and rvalid0 .. rvalid9, 1 bit each); when sel is from 10 to 14, rdata is 0 and rvalid is 0. rdata and rvalid depend on the held slot_r and the inputs only, not on slot, host_en or host_we of this cycle.

blocks.name: cluster_status
blocks.description: Combinational. The inputs are the status bits of 10 cores, one bit each: running0 .. running9, done0 .. done9, error0 .. error9 and diverged0 .. diverged9. running is 1 when any running<k> is 1. done is 1 when every done<k> is 1. error is 1 when any error<k> is 1. diverged is 1 when any diverged<k> is 1. No clock, no reset, no state.

blocks.name: gpu_bridge
blocks.description: Bridge from the SoC's memory stage to the GPU's host bus. Inputs: gpu_we (a store to the GPU window that is really happening), gpu_re (a load from it that is really happening), addr (32 bits, the access address), wdata (32, the store data), memtype (3, the access type: 2 is a word; 6 and 7 are reserved codes that act as a word; every other code is narrower or no access), host_rdata (32) and host_rvalid from the host bus. Outputs: host_en, host_we, host_addr (32), host_wdata (32) to the host bus, and rdata (32), what a load from the window returns. Translation, with off = addr bits 23:0: off from 000000 to 00FFFF hexadecimal is mapped to host address 30000000 | off bits 15:0 (control registers); 010000 to 0107FF to off bits 10:0, zero-extended (instruction memory); 020000 to 021FFF to 10000000 | off bits 12:0 (global memory); 030000 to 030FFF to 20000000 | off bits 11:0 (shared memory); 100000 to 1257FF to 40000000 | off bits 17:0 (video memory); 140000 to 1657FF to 40040000 | off bits 17:0 (depth memory); 180000 to 1807FF to 50000000 | off bits 10:0 (texture). Every other off is unmapped. host_addr is the mapped host address, 0 when unmapped. Outputs, at once: word = (memtype is 2, 6 or 7); host_we = mapped & gpu_we & word; host_en = host_we | (mapped & gpu_re); host_wdata = wdata; rdata = host_rdata when host_rvalid is 1, otherwise the register rdata_r. So a narrower store, or any access to an unmapped offset, is dropped. One register, rdata_r (32 bits): on each rising edge it becomes 0 when rst is 1, else takes host_rdata when host_rvalid is 1, else keeps its value. The host bus answers a read one cycle after the request (host_rvalid = 1 then), so a load returns the result of the previous GPU read and starts its own: a driver reads a GPU address twice and keeps the second value, and two loads in consecutive cycles work because the second sees host_rdata directly.
